idiom_name: capability/context value of primitives passed into a behaviour trait method (Sandbox<'a>, Commands-style)
implementation_notes: Rust has no implementation inheritance at all: the book states there is no way to define a struct that inherits the parent's fields and method implementations, and that reuse is achieved instead with default trait methods and composition. The sandbox is therefore a value rather than a base class - the primitives become methods on a narrow context type (struct Sandbox<'a> { audio, fx, ... }) and a behaviour is any type implementing a one-method trait, such as fn activate(&mut self, sb: &mut Sandbox<'_>), so the behaviour can only do what it was handed; an ECS reaches the same shape by giving systems Commands, Query and Res instead of the whole world. Visibility replaces protected: pub(crate) or a sealed trait keeps the primitives inside the module or crate, and nothing in the language enforces 'compose only these operations' beyond the type of the parameter. Reserve the trait-plus-context form for behaviour that shares state or registration plumbing; when behaviour is data, an enum with a match is simpler.
pitfalls: A &mut Sandbox borrows the world exclusively, so a behaviour cannot read unrelated state in the same call; the capability must be split into narrower fields or an ECS-style query abstraction, otherwise the borrow checker rejects designs that a base class with hidden state would have allowed.

Generics monomorphise (static dispatch, no vtable) while Box<dyn Power> gives the heterogeneous registry; the sandbox method must stay dyn-compatible (no generic parameters, no returning Self) or the registry form stops compiling.
pub(crate) is not protected: a sandbox type that must be shared across crate boundaries loses the wall, and a sealed trait only prevents implementations, not direct calls to the primitives.

The context is passed by reference and cannot be stored for later without fighting lifetimes, so deferred behaviour (callbacks, spawned tasks) needs the data copied into the behaviour or the sandbox reconstructed at the point of use.
